_meta.note: Re-audit of the S265 sources. (1) Terminal-Bench 4.0: the WebFetch summary S265 relied on returned only the top 5 of a 14-row board; the remaining 9 rows are parsed from the raw HTML table — the same partial-slice failure S265c found on NYT Connections. (2) SRE-Bench paper: Figures 2 and 4 were dismissed in S265 as figure-only, but the pdftotext extraction contains their full numeric values (5 models x 9 language/domain columns; 5 models x 8 protection presets); ingested as sub-metric ids on the 0-6 rubric scale. (3) Terminal-Universe (Qwen, 2026-09-04) was skipped in S265 as 'research SFT checkpoints', which was too broad: the paper's own model Terminal-Universe-27B is a named Qwen release, EvoCode-Bench v2 is a new benchmark absent from the DB, and the Qwen3.5-27B base rows are net-new. Qwen3.7-Max's TB2.0 69.7 / TB2.1 74.5 in the paper match the existing DB rows exactly, which also confirms `terminal_bench_2` is the TB2.0 id. The other research checkpoints in Table 3 (TerminalTraj-32B, TermiGen-32B, Nemotron-Terminal-32B, TMax-27B, ...) are still left out. NOT INGESTED after re-audit: Terminal-Bench-Science's TB2.1/TB3.0/TBS comparison table — its 'TB2.1' column (Fable 5 83.8, Opus 4.8 78.9, Terra 78.4, Luna 75.7) does not match the DB's TB2.1 rows (88.0/82.7/87.4/84.7), so the column identities cannot be confirmed from the flattened RSC text and the candidate TB3.0 values (42.7/34.4/33.8/21.1/20.8/14.3) are withheld; its per-domain chart (15 values, 3 models) because the domain labels are not recoverable from the payload; the CRI page beyond Opus 5 (chart only, no data in scripts/img/iframe); openai.com/index/gpt-6-astra (HTTP 403 to curl); the K2 Horizon product page (no tables or specs beyond the blog). BenchLM ARC-AGI-3 was re-checked and is complete at 12 rows.

benchmarks.description: EvoCode-Bench v2 (Shen et al., 2026a): sequential development requests in a persistent workspace. MT@4 uses fail-stop scoring — a run is credited only for the consecutive rounds it completes, averaged within each task and then across tasks. Higher better.
